arithmetic: exact integers only (det4 == 0 for forbidden 4-sets); no floating point

firstmove_question.statement: g(empty)=mex{g({p})}. So g(empty)=0 forces g({p})!=0 for every p, i.e. W_n = {} and all n^2 first moves lose.
firstmove_question.consequence: A second-player-win square board has ZERO winning first moves; the mixed case (some losing first moves) is impossible for it.
firstmove_question.n7_verdict: SUPPORTED-BY-CONSTRUCTION: W_7 = {} ; all 49 first moves lose. No enumeration required.
firstmove_question.n8_verdict: SUPPORTED-BY-CONSTRUCTION: W_8 = {} ; all 64 first moves lose. No enumeration required.
firstmove_question.caveat: This settles the WIN/LOSS classification, not the nimber values. The nimber multiset {g({p})} is a strictly finer datum and is what Part 2 computes for n=7.
